intro: Lacrosse was created by Indigenous peoples of North America — the Haudenosaunee call it the Creator's Game — long before Europeans arrived. Players use sticks with a netted pocket to catch, carry and throw a solid rubber ball, and shoot at a goal guarded by a goalkeeper. Today it is played in several forms; World Lacrosse governs the sport internationally and introduced the fast, small-sided 'sixes' format used at the 2028 Olympics.
inThirtySeconds: Carry the ball in your stick's netted pocket and shoot it into the goal.
No one may touch the ball with their hands except the goalkeeper in the crease.
Attackers can't step into the circle around the goal (the crease).
A shot clock keeps play moving; fouls send players to the penalty box.
objective: Score more goals than the opponent.

facts.players: Men's field: 10 v 10 · Women's: 12 v 12 · Sixes: 6 v 6
facts.duration: Four quarters (length depends on format and level)

scoring.label: Goal
scoring.detail: The ball fully crosses the goal line. Some leagues award 2 points for long-range shots.

variants.name: Field
variants.description: The traditional outdoor game with large teams and a full-size field.

variants.name: Sixes
variants.description: A fast 6-a-side format on a smaller field with a short shot clock; chosen for the Olympics.

rules.title: Sticks, not hands
rules.summary: Field players must not touch the ball with their hands; it is carried, passed and shot with the stick.
rules.body: Players 'cradle' the ball — rocking the stick — to keep it in the pocket while running. Kicking the ball is allowed to move it, but goals cannot be kicked in.

rules.title: The crease
rules.summary: Attackers may not enter the circle around the goal (the crease). Inside it, the goalkeeper is protected.
rules.body: A goal does not count if the shooter lands in the crease. Defenders may pass through the crease but must not hold the ball there for long.

rules.title: Shot clock
rules.summary: Teams must shoot on goal within the shot clock, which is much shorter in sixes.
rules.body: The clock resets when a shot hits the goal or goalkeeper. In field lacrosse, teams must also advance the ball over the midfield line within a time limit.

rules.title: Stick checks and body checks
rules.summary: Defenders may hit an opponent's stick to dislodge the ball. In men's field lacrosse, body checks are allowed on the ball carrier within limits; women's lacrosse and sixes restrict contact far more.
rules.body: Checks must be below the neck and from the front or side. Slashing (swinging at the body), cross-checking with the shaft and hits to the head are personal fouls.

rules.title: Personal and technical fouls
rules.summary: Technical fouls (like holding or offside) usually cost possession or 30 seconds in the box; personal fouls cost one to three minutes.
rules.body: The penalised team plays a player short — giving the opponents a man-up opportunity. Women's lacrosse uses free positions instead of a penalty box for many fouls.

fouls.name: Crease violation
fouls.description: Attacker steps into the goal crease.

fouls.name: Slashing
fouls.description: Swinging the stick at an opponent's body.
fouls.consequence: Personal foul, time in the penalty box

flow.title: Face-off / draw
flow.description: Possession starts with a face-off (men) or a draw (women).

flow.title: Settled attack
flow.description: Teams work the ball around the crease.

flow.title: Transition
flow.description: Fast breaks after saves and turnovers.

positions.name: Attack
positions.role: Scorers who play near the opponents' goal.

positions.name: Midfield
positions.role: Run both ends of the field.

positions.name: Defence
positions.role: Often carry long sticks to check attackers.

positions.name: Goalkeeper
positions.role: Guards a 6 ft square goal with a large-headed stick.

field.name: Field
field.dimensions: Men's field: about 110 m × 60 m; sixes uses a much smaller field

glossary.definition: Rocking the stick to keep the ball in the pocket.
The protected circle around the goal.
Restart where two players contest the ball at midfield.
Playing with an extra player after an opponent's penalty.

funFacts: The Haudenosaunee Nationals compete internationally as their own nation in World Lacrosse events.
Lacrosse returns to the Olympic programme at Los Angeles 2028 in the sixes format.
